books.section: B. The Fall of the Berlin Wall and the End of the Cold War
The Presidency of George H. W. Bush

stem: The photograph best illustrates which of the following developments?

options.text: The construction of the Berlin Wall by the Soviet Union in 1961
options.misconception: The Wall was built in 1961, but the photograph shows it being taken apart, not built.

options.text: The collapse of Communist rule in Eastern Europe in 1989
The signing of the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty in 1987
options.misconception: The INF Treaty limited missiles; it was signed two years before this photograph was taken.

options.text: The reunification of Germany under the Weimar Republic in 1919
options.misconception: The Weimar Republic dates to 1919, seventy years before this photograph, and it did not reunify Germany.

rationales.A: The photograph shows the Wall coming down, not going up. Background: the Wall had divided Berlin since 1961.
rationales.B: The photograph shows ordinary Berliners chipping pieces from the Wall as souvenirs in November 1989, after East Germany opened the border. Background: within weeks, Communist governments across Eastern Europe fell.
rationales.C: The treaty is not visible in the photograph. Background: the INF Treaty of 1987 eliminated intermediate-range missiles; it did not touch the Wall.
rationales.D: The Weimar Republic belongs to the era after World War I. Background: Germany reunified in 1990, after the Wall fell, not in 1919.
rationales.general:
1. Look at what the man is doing. He stands on a ladder, chipping pieces from a graffiti-covered wall, while a crowd watches below.
2. That is souvenir-hunting at a wall coming down, not a wall going up.
3. Background: East Germany opened the border in November 1989, and Berliners from both sides began tearing the Wall apart.
4. The Wall had divided Berlin since 1961, so its demolition marked the collapse of Communist rule.
Remember: a crowd dismantling a wall means an order is falling, not rising.

stimulus.source_note: Photograph by Staff Sergeant F. Lee Corkran, U.S. Department of Defense, November 14, 1989, Potsdamer Platz, Berlin. Public domain (U.S. federal government work).
stimulus.text: Photograph of a man on a ladder using a hammer and chisel to chip a piece from the Berlin Wall at Potsdamer Platz, Berlin, November 1989. The Wall's western face is covered in colorful graffiti, and a crowd watches from below.

figures.caption: A Berliner chips a souvenir from the Berlin Wall, Potsdamer Platz, November 1989
figures.alt: A man on a ladder chips at the graffiti-covered Berlin Wall with a hammer and chisel while a crowd watches below
